# spatialkit

spatialkit draws analysis regions, which it calls cells, from where your
observations are, instead of borrowing boundaries drawn for other
purposes, and summarises point data onto them with a count, a standard
error and a pooled value for every cell. It then scores regression
models on cross-validation folds that hold out whole blocks of space,
and marks where a fitted map extrapolates.

## The problem this solves

You have observations at points and need values over areas. The usual
move is to borrow boundaries that already exist: ZIP code areas, census
tracts, counties, sales territories. They were drawn for mail delivery,
enumeration or politics, so part of any answer aggregated onto them
comes from the partition. This is the modifiable areal unit problem: the
same observations, aggregated under different boundaries, can give
different conclusions.

spatialkit draws the cells from the data, in three steps:

1.  Pick a cell count.
    [`resolution_profile()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/resolution_profile.md)
    and
    [`select_resolution()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/select_resolution.md)
    set it from a size of 4.5 observations per cell by default, and
    report the leave-one-out error of the cell values. Given a ladder of
    counts, the profile scores each one against the spatial structure of
    the observations.
2.  Place the cells.
    [`get_voronoi_seeds()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/get_voronoi_seeds.md)
    places seeds by density-weighted k-means, so cells are small where
    observations are dense, and
    [`build_tessellation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/build_tessellation.md)
    grows Voronoi cells from them (or lays hex or square cells, or
    Delaunay triangles), clipped to your study area.
    [`build_tessellation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/build_tessellation.md)
    numbers the cells from their geometry, so the same seeds in a
    different row order give the same cell IDs.
3.  Summarise.
    [`summarize_by_cell()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/summarize_by_cell.md)
    gives each cell a count, a mean with its standard error, and a
    pooled value: the cell’s mean pulled toward the mean of the
    observations in the 8 nearest cells (nearest by the centroid of
    their observations). When the cell means stand in for a population
    mean, it can correct the standard errors for autocorrelation within
    the cells, which on a correlated field can double them or more.

The first figure shows a simulated field on 280 random sites in North
Carolina, aggregated onto three kinds of cells, about 30 of each:
Voronoi cells from density-weighted seeds, a hex grid and a square grid.

![Four maps of North Carolina: a simulated field at 280 sites, and its
cell means on 30 Voronoi cells from density-weighted seeds, on a hex
grid and on a square
grid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elkronos/gis_modeling_toolkit/main/man/figures/readme-tessellations.png) 

The next figure cuts the same field at three cell counts, each cell
showing its pooled value.
[`resolution_profile()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/resolution_profile.md)
scores each count by the leave-one-out error of the pooled values at
that count. The error is 0.33 at 12 cells, 0.18 at 62 cells (the count
the default size of 4.5 observations per cell gives) and 0.18 at 140
cells (two per cell). The 12 cells blur the hotspot in the east. At 140
cells the error is within one standard error of the default’s.
[`vignette("resolution")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/resolution.md)
covers how the count is chosen.

![Four maps of North Carolina: the simulated field at 280 sites, and its
pooled cell values at 12, 62 and 140 Voronoi cells, where 62 is the
default
count](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elkronos/gis_modeling_toolkit/main/man/figures/readme-resolution.png) 

The second half of the package tests the result. Three model backends
(random forest, GWR and a Bayesian GP) sit behind one `spatial_fit`
class, so they can be scored on the same folds. Cross-validation holds
out whole blocks, of a grid by default, which can be sized from the
data’s own autocorrelation range or matched to the locations a map will
predict at. An area-of-applicability estimate marks where the resulting
score applies. All of it is built on
[`sf`](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/), and each function that measures
a distance moves a lon/lat layer into a projected CRS first.

Random folds put a test point’s neighbours in the training set, so a
model that can memorise location is scored on points it has nearly seen.
Block folds hold out whole blocks instead; the quick start below shows
the difference in RMSE.

![Two maps of North Carolina: 280 sites coloured by fold, mixed at
random on the left and grouped into spatial blocks on the
right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elkronos/gis_modeling_toolkit/main/man/figures/readme-spatial-cv.png) 

## Scope

- **Regression, with one exception.**
  [`fit_rf_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_rf_model.md)
  and
  [`fit_gwr_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_gwr_model.md)
  fit a numeric response and refuse a logical, factor or character one;
  [`fit_gwr_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_gwr_model.md)
  also refuses an integer-coded two-valued response and points to
  [`GWmodel::ggwr.basic()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/GWmodel/man/ggwr.basic.html).
  The exception is
  [`fit_bayesian_spatial_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_bayesian_spatial_model.md),
  which also fits a binary response under
  [`brms::bernoulli()`](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/reference/brmsfamily.html),
  and a factor or character response under
  [`brms::categorical()`](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/reference/brmsfamily.html)
  or an ordinal family.
  [`cv_bayes()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_bayes.md)
  refuses the categorical and ordinal families, because it scores one
  predicted number per row.
- **Vector data only.** There is no raster input or output:
  [`predict_surface()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/predict_surface.md)
  returns an `sf` POINT layer, which you convert yourself if you need a
  `SpatRaster`. The models work on points:
  [`prep_model_data()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/prep_model_data.md)
  and
  [`coerce_to_points()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/coerce_to_points.md)
  reduce lines and polygons to points.
- **No areal or lattice models.** Moran’s I here tests residuals for
  spatial structure. There is no CAR, SAR or spatial-lag fitter.
- **No spatio-temporal folds.** Every fold scheme is spatial; none holds
  out time.

## Installation

``` r

install.packages("spatialkit")
```

The development version installs from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("elkronos/gis_modeling_toolkit")
```

`sf`, `dplyr`, `logger`, `digest` and `FNN` install with it. Optional
packages switch on the model backends, variograms and plots; [Get
started](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/getting-started.html)
lists which does what. If you are upgrading from 2.0.0, the
[changelog](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/news/index.html)
lists the defaults that change results and the argument that restores
each.

## Quick start

A simulated field of 400 observations in a 1,000 m square, with one weak
measured predictor `w`:

``` r

library(sf)
library(spatialkit)

set.seed(42)
n  <- 400
xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000))
D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy))
xy$w <- rnorm(n)
# Mostly a smooth spatial field (exponential, effective range 3 x 80 = 240 m),
# with the weak predictor on top.
xy$z <- 0.5 * xy$w +
  as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 80) + diag(1e-8, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) +
  rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)
site <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)
```

Set the cell count, draw Voronoi cells from the data and summarise onto
them:

``` r

size <- select_resolution(resolution_profile(site, "z"))
size
#> Resolution by size: 89 cells
#>   size        : 4.5 rows per cell, the default (obs_per_cell); 400 rows / 89 cells = 4.49
#>   cells       : density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours)
#>   estimate    : pooled toward the 8 nearest cells
#>   at this size: 0.0% of the rows are alone in their cell; median own weight 0.78
#>   loo         : 0.912 (one cell for the layer: 1.5)
#>   note        : the count is set by obs_per_cell = 4.5, the default; no
#>                 criterion chose it.

seeds <- get_voronoi_seeds(n = size, sample_points = site)
tess  <- build_tessellation(seeds,
                            boundary = clip_target_for(site, quiet = TRUE),
                            method = "voronoi", quiet = TRUE)
asg   <- assign_features_to_polygons(site, tess$cells,
                                     polygon_id_col = "cell_id")
cells <- summarize_by_cell(asg, "z", id_col = "cell_id", cells_sf = tess$cells)

head(st_drop_geometry(cells)[, c("cell_id", "n", "resp_mean_z", "..se_resp_z",
                                 "..pooled_resp_z")], 4)
#>   cell_id n resp_mean_z ..se_resp_z ..pooled_resp_z
#> 1       1 4   1.3680408   0.3289247       1.0626423
#> 2       2 3  -0.2762594   0.1258383      -0.1086915
#> 3       3 3  -0.9436130   0.5218985      -0.6630103
#> 4       4 5  -1.9008715   0.1581262      -1.4425290
```

The default size gives 89 cells, each holding between 2 and 10
observations. Each row has a count, the cell mean, its standard error
and the pooled value `..pooled_resp_z`, the cell’s mean pulled toward
its neighbours by a weight that grows with the cell’s count
([`?summarize_by_cell`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/summarize_by_cell.md),
“Pooled values”). That standard error is the one for the cell’s own mean
when its points are spread through the cell. When the cell means stand
in for the population mean, `deff = "kish"` widens each standard error
for the correlation inside the cell; on these cells it multiplies them
by 2.2 (median).
[`?summarize_by_cell`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/summarize_by_cell.md)
says which to use when.

Then score a model. A random forest given the coordinates
(`include_coords = TRUE`) can fit the training surface by memorising
location. Score it on random folds and on blocks of at least 250 m, just
above the field’s effective range (this needs `ranger`):

``` r

fr <- make_folds(site, k = 5, method = "random_kfold", seed = 1)
fb <- make_folds(site, k = 5, method = "block_kfold", block_size = 250,
                 seed = 1)

random  <- cv_rf(site, "z", "w", folds = fr, include_coords = TRUE)
blocked <- cv_rf(site, "z", "w", folds = fb, include_coords = TRUE)

c(random = random$overall$RMSE, blocked = blocked$overall$RMSE)
#>    random   blocked 
#> 0.9790119 1.1227029
```

On the same 400 observations and the same model, random folds give an
RMSE of 0.98 and the blocks, built 332 m wide, give 1.12. The data and
the model are the same; the random figure is the error of predicting
among the samples, and the blocked one the error of predicting into gaps
a block wide. A map’s error depends on where it predicts, and
[`fold_separation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fold_separation.md)
compares the folds’ distances from the training data with the map’s. On
real data the range is estimated, by
[`estimate_sac_range()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/estimate_sac_range.md)
or `make_folds(auto_range = TRUE)`;
[`vignette("spatial-cross-validation")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatial-cross-validation.md)
covers that choice.

## The pipeline

Steps 1 to 10 link to their section of the [reference
index](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html),
and every step to the article that shows it.
[`?spatialkit`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatialkit-package.md)
lists the same steps inside R.

| Step | Main functions | Article |
|----|----|----|
| 1\. [Prepare the data](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#prepare-the-data) | [`ensure_projected()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/ensure_projected.md), [`coerce_to_points()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/coerce_to_points.md), [`prep_model_data()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/prep_model_data.md) | [Get started](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/getting-started.html) |
| 2\. [Measure spatial autocorrelation](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#measure-spatial-autocorrelation) | [`estimate_sac_range()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/estimate_sac_range.md) | [Spatial cross-validation](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatial-cross-validation.html) |
| 3\. [Choose a resolution](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#choose-a-resolution) | [`resolution_profile()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/resolution_profile.md), [`select_resolution()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/select_resolution.md) | [Choosing a resolution](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/resolution.html) |
| 4\. [Build the cells](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#build-the-cells) | [`get_voronoi_seeds()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/get_voronoi_seeds.md), [`build_tessellation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/build_tessellation.md) | [Building cells and summarising them](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/cells.html) |
| 5\. [Assign and summarise](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#assign-and-summarise) | [`assign_features_to_polygons()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/assign_features_to_polygons.md), [`summarize_by_cell()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/summarize_by_cell.md) | [Building cells and summarising them](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/cells.html) |
| 6\. [Make folds](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#make-folds) | [`make_folds()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/make_folds.md), [`fold_separation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fold_separation.md) | [Spatial cross-validation](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatial-cross-validation.html) |
| 7\. [Fit a model](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#fit-a-model) | [`fit_rf_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_rf_model.md), [`fit_gwr_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_gwr_model.md), [`fit_bayesian_spatial_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_bayesian_spatial_model.md) | [Fitting and checking models](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/models.html) |
| 8\. [Cross-validate and compare](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#cross-validate-and-compare) | [`cv_rf()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_rf.md), [`cv_gwr()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_gwr.md), [`cv_bayes()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_bayes.md), [`compare_models_cv()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/compare_models_cv.md) | [Spatial cross-validation](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatial-cross-validation.html) |
| 9\. [Choose predictors](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#choose-predictors) | [`select_features_forward()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/select_features_forward.md) | [Fitting and checking models](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/models.html) |
| 10\. [Predict a surface](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/index.html#predict-a-surface) and check where it applies | [`predict_surface()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/predict_surface.md), [`area_of_applicability()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/area_of_applicability.md) | [Fitting and checking models](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/models.html) |
| 11\. Report | [`ensure_stable_poly_id()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/ensure_stable_poly_id.md), [`sf::st_write()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/reference/st_write.html) | [Exporting and reporting results](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/reporting.html) |

## Where to go next

The
[articles](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/index.html),
in reading order:

| Article | What it covers | In R |
|----|----|----|
| [Get started](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/getting-started.html) | Take a layer of points to cells with standard errors, a score from spatial cross-validation and a map that marks where its predictions apply. | [`vignette("getting-started")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/getting-started.md) |
| [Choosing a resolution](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/resolution.html) | Decide how many cells the data support, and pass that count to the tessellation. | [`vignette("resolution")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/resolution.md) |
| [Building cells and summarising them](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/cells.html) | Draw the cells, put each observation in one, and report each cell’s value with the right standard error. | [`vignette("cells")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/cells.md) |
| [Spatial cross-validation](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatial-cross-validation.html) | Choose folds whose score matches the map you will make, size the blocks, and read every part of the result. | [`vignette("spatial-cross-validation")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatial-cross-validation.md) |
| [Fitting and checking models](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/models.html) | Pick a backend or write your own, compare backends on the same folds, check the residuals, and map where the predictions apply. | [`vignette("models")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/models.md) |
| [Exporting and reporting results](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/reporting.html) | Write the cells to a file others can join to, and report the numbers that say how far a cell value or a map can be trusted. | [`vignette("reporting")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/reporting.md) |
| [Worked example: North Carolina](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatialkit_nc_demo.html) | The pipeline on a simulated field over North Carolina, comparing four tessellations, two fold schemes and two backends at cell counts set by hand. | [`vignette("spatialkit_nc_demo")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatialkit_nc_demo.md) |
| [Troubleshooting and performance](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/troubleshooting.html) | The errors and warnings you are most likely to meet, what each means, and how to handle large layers, parallel folds, caches and the log. | [`vignette("troubleshooting")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/troubleshooting.md) |
| [Terms used on these pages](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/glossary.html) | Short definitions of the terms the articles and help pages use. | [`vignette("glossary")`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/glossary.md) |

The numbered scripts in `system.file("scripts", package = "spatialkit")`
run each step on a simulated field; Get started lists them. Report a bug
or ask a question on the [issue
tracker](https://github.com/elkronos/gis_modeling_toolkit/issues); the
[contributing
guide](https://github.com/elkronos/gis_modeling_toolkit/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)
says what to include.

## Citation

``` r

citation("spatialkit")
```

This prints the package entry and the papers behind the methods
spatialkit implements. Cite the paper as well as the package if you rely
on
[`area_of_applicability()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/area_of_applicability.md)
(Meyer and Pebesma 2021), `make_folds(method = "nndm")` (Milà et
al. 2022) or `make_folds(method = "knndm")` (Linnenbrink et al. 2024).
Do the same for the model backends you use: the Hilbert space
approximation in
[`fit_bayesian_spatial_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_bayesian_spatial_model.md)
(Riutort-Mayol et al. 2023), permutation importance in
[`fit_rf_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_rf_model.md)
(Strobl et al. 2007), coordinates as predictors and blocked validation
in
[`fit_rf_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_rf_model.md)
and
[`cv_rf()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_rf.md)
(Meyer et al. 2019), and GWR, whose kernels and diagnostics follow
`GWmodel` (Lu et al. 2014).

# Package index

## Start here

The pipeline in order, the function for each step, and where each
default comes from.

- [`spatialkit`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatialkit-package.md)
  [`spatialkit-package`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatialkit-package.md)
  : spatialkit: Spatial Tessellation, Modelling, and Cross-Validation
  Toolkit

## Prepare the data

Put the observations in a projected CRS as points, and see how the
package reads input geometry.

- [`ensure_projected()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/ensure_projected.md)
  : Project an sf object to a CRS suited to its extent
- [`harmonize_crs()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/harmonize_crs.md)
  : Bring two spatial objects to one CRS
- [`coerce_to_points()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/coerce_to_points.md)
  : Reduce each geometry to one representative point
- [`prep_model_data()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/prep_model_data.md)
  : Prepare an sf layer for model fitting
- [`` `[`( ``*`<spatialkit_rows>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/sub-.spatialkit_rows.md)
  : Subset a layer that carries a row record
- [`spatialkit-geometry`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatialkit-geometry.md)
  : How input geometry is read

## Measure spatial autocorrelation

The distance over which observations stay correlated. It can size the
cross-validation blocks (`make_folds(auto_range = TRUE)`) and sets a
floor on the number of cells, which
`select_resolution(criterion = "reliability")` and
`resolution_profile(range_floor = TRUE)` apply.

- [`estimate_sac_range()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/estimate_sac_range.md)
  [`print(`*`<sac_range>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/estimate_sac_range.md)
  : Estimate the spatial autocorrelation range from data
- [`sac_nugget()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/sac_nugget.md)
  : Extract the nugget of an estimated autocorrelation range
- [`plot(`*`<sac_range>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot.sac_range.md)
  : Plot an estimated spatial autocorrelation range

## Choose a resolution

How many cells the data support, and the counts the chosen criterion
scores within `tol` of its best (the flat region).

- [`resolution_profile()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/resolution_profile.md)
  [`print(`*`<resolution_profile>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/resolution_profile.md)
  : Score candidate cell counts on several criteria
- [`select_resolution()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/select_resolution.md)
  : Choose a cell count from a resolution profile
- [`summary(`*`<resolution_profile>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/summary.resolution_profile.md)
  : Compare every criterion's pick on a resolution profile
- [`plot(`*`<resolution_profile>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot.resolution_profile.md)
  : Plot a resolution profile
- [`determine_optimal_levels()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/determine_optimal_levels.md)
  : Choose a cell count from the elbow of the k-means WSS curve

## Build the cells

Voronoi, hex, square and Delaunay cells. Start with
[`build_tessellation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/build_tessellation.md).
Hex and square cells need a boundary;
[`clip_target_for()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/clip_target_for.md)
builds one from the points. The seed functions place the points Voronoi
cells are drawn around, and the lower-level builders draw cells of one
kind or number them.

- [`build_tessellation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/build_tessellation.md)
  : Build Voronoi, triangle, hex or square cells from points
- [`clip_target_for()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/clip_target_for.md)
  : Build the area to tessellate within, from points or a boundary
- [`plot_tessellation_map()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot_tessellation_map.md)
  : Plot a tessellation map with optional boundary, seeds, and features

### Place Voronoi seeds

- [`get_voronoi_seeds()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/get_voronoi_seeds.md)
  : Place seeds for a Voronoi tessellation
- [`voronoi_seeds_kmeans()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/voronoi_seeds_kmeans.md)
  : Place seeds at k-means cluster centres
- [`voronoi_seeds_random()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/voronoi_seeds_random.md)
  : Place seeds at random inside a boundary

### Lower-level builders and IDs

- [`create_voronoi_polygons()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/create_voronoi_polygons.md)
  : Build Voronoi cells around points
- [`create_grid_polygons()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/create_grid_polygons.md)
  : Create square or hexagonal grid polygons over a boundary
- [`create_grid_polygons_cached()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/create_grid_polygons_cached.md)
  : Create and cache grid polygons over a boundary
- [`ensure_stable_poly_id()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/ensure_stable_poly_id.md)
  : Give cells IDs that follow their position

## Assign and summarise

Put each observation in a cell, reduce to one row per cell with a count,
a standard error and a pooled value, and read cell values at other
locations.
[`kriging_adequacy()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/kriging_adequacy.md)
checks the cell mean against block kriging.

- [`assign_features_to_polygons()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/assign_features_to_polygons.md)
  : Assign features to cells and attach a cell ID
- [`summarize_by_cell()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/summarize_by_cell.md)
  : Summarise assigned points by cell, with standard errors and pooled
  values
- [`cell_values_at()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cell_values_at.md)
  : Read cell values at new locations
- [`kriging_adequacy()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/kriging_adequacy.md)
  : Check whether block kriging would improve cell means

## Make folds

Spatial cross-validation folds, the block size, and how far the held-out
points sit from the training data, beside the map’s locations when you
pass them.

- [`make_folds()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/make_folds.md)
  : Create spatial cross-validation folds
- [`plot_folds()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot_folds.md)
  : Map a cross-validation fold scheme
- [`fold_separation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fold_separation.md)
  : Measure how far the held-out points sit from their training data
- [`cv_block_size_sweep()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_block_size_sweep.md)
  [`plot(`*`<block_size_sweep>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_block_size_sweep.md)
  : Cross-validate at a ladder of block sizes

## Fit a model

Random forest, GWR and Bayesian GP backends behind one `spatial_fit`
class, the length-scale bounds the GP uses, and the constructor for a
backend of your own.

- [`fit_rf_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_rf_model.md)
  : Fit a random forest with ranger
- [`fit_gwr_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_gwr_model.md)
  : Fit a geographically weighted regression (GWR)
- [`fit_bayesian_spatial_model()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/fit_bayesian_spatial_model.md)
  : Fit a Bayesian Gaussian-process regression with brms
- [`gp_lengthscale_bounds()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/gp_lengthscale_bounds.md)
  : Compute length-scale bounds for a squared-exponential GP
- [`new_spatial_fit()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/new_spatial_fit.md)
  : Build a spatial_fit object for a backend of your own

## Use a fitted model

[`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html),
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) and
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) for any fit;
[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html),
[`fitted()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/fitted.values.html) and
[`residuals()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/residuals.html) for each
backend; and [`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html) for GWR and
the Bayesian GP, since a forest has no coefficients. A forest’s fitted
values and residuals are out-of-bag.

- [`print(`*`<spatial_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/print.spatial_fit.md)
  [`print(`*`<rf_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/print.spatial_fit.md)
  : Print a fitted model
- [`summary(`*`<spatial_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/summary.spatial_fit.md)
  : Summarise a fitted model
- [`plot(`*`<spatial_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot.spatial_fit.md)
  : Plot a fitted spatial model
- [`predict(`*`<gwr_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-predict.md)
  [`predict(`*`<bayesian_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-predict.md)
  [`predict(`*`<rf_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-predict.md)
  : Predict from a fitted model
- [`fitted(`*`<gwr_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-fitted.md)
  [`fitted(`*`<bayesian_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-fitted.md)
  [`fitted(`*`<rf_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-fitted.md)
  : Extract the fitted values of a fitted model
- [`residuals(`*`<gwr_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-residuals.md)
  [`residuals(`*`<bayesian_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-residuals.md)
  [`residuals(`*`<rf_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-residuals.md)
  : Extract the residuals of a fitted model
- [`coef(`*`<gwr_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-coef.md)
  [`coef(`*`<bayesian_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-coef.md)
  [`coef(`*`<rf_fit>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatial_fit-coef.md)
  : Extract the coefficients of a fitted model

## Check a fit in sample

Metrics on the training data (out-of-bag for a forest), and residual
Moran’s I, which tests for spatial structure the model left behind.
In-sample metrics do not compare across backends; compare backends with
[`compare_models_cv()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/compare_models_cv.md).
[`model_metrics()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/model_metrics.md),
[`evaluate_insample()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/evaluate_insample.md)
and
[`compare_models()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/compare_models.md)
also score rows you held out, passed as `newdata`.

- [`model_metrics()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/model_metrics.md)
  : Compute goodness-of-fit metrics for a fitted model
- [`evaluate_insample()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/evaluate_insample.md)
  : Compute the metrics of several fitted models
- [`compare_models()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/compare_models.md)
  : Compare fitted models in sample
- [`residual_morans_i()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/residual_morans_i.md)
  : Test the residuals of a fitted model for spatial autocorrelation
- [`print(`*`<morans_i>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/print.morans_i.md)
  : Print a residual Moran's I result

## Cross-validate and compare

Score a model on held-out blocks, compare backends on the same folds,
and plot the per-fold spread and interval calibration.

- [`cv_spatial()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_spatial.md)
  : Cross-validate any learner with spatial folds
- [`cv_rf()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_rf.md)
  : Cross-validate a random forest with spatial folds
- [`cv_gwr()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_gwr.md)
  : Cross-validate a GWR with spatial folds
- [`cv_bayes()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/cv_bayes.md)
  : Cross-validate a Bayesian GP with spatial folds
- [`compare_models_cv()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/compare_models_cv.md)
  : Compare models on the same cross-validation folds
- [`plot_cv_metrics()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot_cv_metrics.md)
  : Plot one cross-validation metric fold by fold
- [`plot_calibration()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot_calibration.md)
  : Plot the interval calibration of a Bayesian cross-validation

## Choose predictors

Forward selection scored on spatial folds for any backend, and an AICc
search over predictor sets for GWR.

- [`select_features_forward()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/select_features_forward.md)
  : Select predictors by forward selection on spatial folds
- [`plot(`*`<feature_selection>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot.feature_selection.md)
  : Plot the path of a forward feature selection
- [`gwr_model_selection()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/gwr_model_selection.md)
  [`print(`*`<gwr_model_selection>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/gwr_model_selection.md)
  : Select GWR predictors by forward selection on AICc
- [`plot(`*`<gwr_model_selection>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot.gwr_model_selection.md)
  : Plot a GWR model selection

## Predict a surface

Predict onto a regular grid, and mark the locations whose predictor
values are too unlike the training data for the cross-validated score to
hold there.

- [`predict_surface()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/predict_surface.md)
  : Predict a fitted model onto a regular grid
- [`area_of_applicability()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/area_of_applicability.md)
  : Mark where a model's predictions apply
- [`print(`*`<aoa>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/print.aoa.md)
  : Print an area-of-applicability result
- [`plot(`*`<aoa>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/plot.aoa.md)
  : Plot the dissimilarity distribution behind an area of applicability

## Set options, catch conditions and clear caches

The console log, the two work limits, every warning and error class the
package raises, and two in-session caches. To free memory, clear the
grid cache that
[`create_grid_polygons_cached()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/create_grid_polygons_cached.md)
fills; clear a Bayesian fit’s fitted-value cache after editing its
`brmsfit` by hand.

- [`spatialkit_quiet()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatialkit_quiet.md)
  : Turn the console log off or on
- [`spatialkit-options`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatialkit-options.md)
  : Options that bound the work of a search or a fit
- [`spatialkit-conditions`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/spatialkit-conditions.md)
  : Warnings and errors the package raises
- [`clear_grid_cache()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/clear_grid_cache.md)
  : Clear the in-session grid cache
- [`clear_fitted_cache()`](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/reference/clear_fitted_cache.md)
  : Clear the cached fitted values of a Bayesian GP fit

# Articles

### Get started

- [Get
  started](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/getting-started.md):

  Take a layer of points to cells with standard errors, a score from
  spatial cross-validation and a map that marks where its predictions
  apply.

### Step by step

One step of the pipeline per article, in the order you take them.

- [Choosing a
  resolution](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/resolution.md):

  Decide how many cells the data support, and pass that count to the
  tessellation.

- [Building cells and summarising
  them](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/cells.md):

  Draw the cells, put each observation in one, and report each cell’s
  value with the right standard error.

- [Spatial
  cross-validation](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatial-cross-validation.md):

  Choose folds whose score matches the map you will make, size the
  blocks, and read every part of the result.

- [Fitting and checking
  models](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/models.md):

  Pick a backend or write your own, compare backends on the same folds,
  check the residuals, and map where the predictions apply.

- [Exporting and reporting
  results](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/reporting.md):

  Write the cells to a file others can join to, and report the numbers
  that say how far a cell value or a map can be trusted.

### Worked example

- [Worked example: North
  Carolina](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/spatialkit_nc_demo.md):

  The pipeline on a simulated field over North Carolina, comparing four
  tessellations, two fold schemes and two backends at cell counts set by
  hand.

### Help

Pages to consult when a step fails or a term is unclear.

- [Troubleshooting and
  performance](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/troubleshooting.md):

  The errors and warnings you are most likely to meet, what each means,
  and how to handle large layers, parallel folds, caches and the log.

- [Terms used on these
  pages](https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/articles/glossary.md):

  Short definitions of the terms the articles and help pages use.
